key_insight: A sharp-edged infinitely thin disk in a rarefied gas generates a radiometric force that grows with Knudsen number, while its terminal velocity changes nonmonotonically and slightly overshoots the free-molecular limit at intermediate rarefaction.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a validated kinetic-theory reference for designing and analyzing micro- and nanoscale devices where thermal asymmetry and edge effects drive motion in rarefied flows.
method: Solved the linearized BGK Boltzmann equation with diffuse reflection on a freely translating thin circular disk.
Used a characteristic-based scheme to capture edge-induced discontinuities in the velocity distribution.
Applied far-field asymptotics for the unbounded domain and validated force results with the symmetric relation.
evidence_signal: The study reports force, terminal velocity, flow, and stress fields over a wide Knudsen-number range, with the radiometric force scaling as Kn^3/2 in the continuum limit and tending to a constant in the free-molecular limit.
watch_item: Accurate resolution of the sharp-edge discontinuity is essential; under-resolving the near-edge stress can distort the predicted radiometric force, especially near the continuum regime.
paper_title: Radiometer effect on an infinitely thin circular disk
